subject: Meadow Labs: sustained latency & error spike — request for remediation and commercial resolution
messages:
From: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@meadowlabs.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@meadowlabs.com>, Gordon Lee <gordon.lee@meadowlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [Meadow Labs] sudden 95th pctl latency jump + 5xxs — urgent

Irene,

We're seeing a sustained regression across several inference endpoints since ~03:30 PST this morning: 95th percentile latency for our main route jumped from ~220ms to ~1.1s and 5xx rates have climbed to ~3.0% (was <0.1%). Throughput dropped ~18% for the VM pool serving our highest-concurrency customers. This is impacting live customers and our support queue is filling fast.

Attached is a short CSV with request-level samples and a few example traces (meadow_latency_sample.csv). Can you confirm receipt and whether Redwood has a remediation path immediately available? We need to understand whether this is a runtime regression, model variant fallback issue, or a capacity scheduling problem.

We will escalate internally if we don't have an operational workaround and an expected timeline in the next 60 minutes. Please loop in your on-call/production team and suggest immediate mitigations.

Ari
Ari Jacobs
Head of Product
Meadow Labs

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@meadowlabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Meadow Labs] sudden 95th pctl latency jump + 5xxs — urgent

Thanks Ari — I received your CSV and the traces. I pulled the runtime metrics and we've isolated a pattern of high tail latency on requests that hit cold KV cache lookups combined with an autoscale imbalance in the dedicated pool serving your account.

Immediate actions we've taken (live):
- Shifted Meadow's traffic to a higher-concurrency pool to reduce queuing pressure.
- Disabled a recent optimizer that introduced an aggressive packing behavior for medium-length sequences.
- Increased routing capacity for your region by 15% (temporary burst).

These measures reduced 95th pctl from ~1.1s to ~420ms in the last 12m, but we see residual 5xx spikes when cache misses coincide with peak windows. Our infra team is running a targeted KV cache warm-up and adjusting the batching window to avoid the packing path that caused degraded tail behavior.

Proposed next steps:
1) Immediate exec touchpoint — proposed 30m call with Ari, Samira, Gordon, Ben, and Rishi to align on impact and credits. Are you available 10:00 PST?
2) Full postmortem and root cause analysis to be delivered within 72 hours (outline attached: postmortem-outline.md).
3) Commercial remedy: I'll propose preliminary pro-rated credit options during the call; final credit calculation contingent on RCA and exact impact window.

I realize this is high-impact — I will stay on this until it's fully stabilized and will escalate to the on-call runtime lead as needed.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0124

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@meadowlabs.com>, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:41:12 -0800
Subject: Re: [Meadow Labs] sudden 95th pctl latency jump + 5xxs — urgent

Ari — thanks for flagging and thanks Irene for the quick mitigation. I'm Ben (AM for Meadow). I want to make sure we have the contractual framing in mind while we work the ops side. Quick notes: 
- Our SLA for production inference lists a monthly availability/latency SLO and an error-rate exclusion window; where there's a documented breach we'll propose a service credit per section 4.2 of the contract.
- To speed things up, can you confirm the customer tenant IDs and approximate #requests/min during the impacted window? That will let us produce an initial credit calculation on the call.
- From a retention standpoint: if Meadow is seeing live customer incidents that affect revenue, we will prioritize a commercial remediation that includes a proposal to offset billing for the impacted month. I'll bring the finance contact on the call if needed.

Proposed credit approach (preliminary): pro-rated service credit for the impacted minutes, plus an up-to-25% goodwill credit for any sustained unresolved degradation pending RCA. We'll refine the exact number once we quantify requests and error-rate delta.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@meadowlabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@meadowlabs.com>, Gordon Lee <gordon.lee@meadowlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:10:35 -0800
Subject: Re: [Meadow Labs] sudden 95th pctl latency jump + 5xxs — urgent

On Thu, Nov 26, 2026 at 9:41 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ari — thanks for flagging and thanks Irene for the quick mitigation. I'm Ben (AM for Meadow). I want to make sure we have the contractual framing in mind while we work the ops side. Quick notes: 
> - Our SLA for production inference lists a monthly availability/latency SLO and an error-rate exclusion window; where there's a documented breach we'll propose a service credit per section 4.2 of the contract.

Irene/Ben — appreciate the rapid responses. This incident has already triggered executive attention here; our CEO is asking what concrete commercial remediation you will propose to our CFO. We need a precise number, not just ranges, for the impacted hours (03:30–05:10 PST) across our production endpoints. If we don't have a firm commitment soon we'll have to escalate through procurement.

For reference: approximate traffic on the impacted tenant was 4,200 reqs/min at peak. I can provide exact tenant IDs and logs if that helps; Samira is on this thread and will share more detail.

Ari

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@meadowlabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, Samira Patel <samira@meadowlabs.com>, Gordon Lee <gordon.lee@meadowlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Meadow Labs] sudden 95th pctl latency jump + 5xxs — urgent

Ari, Samira, Gordon — thanks for the details and your patience while we validated the full impact window. Below is a succinct remediation & commercial proposal for executive review.

Operational summary (final):
- Impact window: 2026-11-26 03:30 PST — 2026-11-26 05:10 PST (100 minutes).
- Peak requests: ~4,200 reqs/min (as reported).
- Measured 5xx delta: +2.9% average across affected endpoints during impact window.
- Root cause (preliminary): aggressive packing optimizer + cold KV cache warmups + autoscaler threshold tuning that allowed a transient queue buildup. Full RCA being compiled; final report in 72 hours.

Commercial remediation (proposal):
1) Service credit: pro-rated credit for the impacted 100 minutes based on your committed plan usage: this equates to XX.XX% of your November invoice (we will calculate using tenant IDs and raw request counts).
2) Goodwill credit: an additional fixed credit equal to 15% of the impacted charge for November to recognize business disruption.
3) Contract amendment: Redwood will offer a one-time addendum to the contract to clarify burst capacity thresholds and introduce an automatic alerting SLA to shorten detection windows. We'll provide a DocuSign-ready amendment link for review.

Attachments: proposed-credit-calculation.xlsx (spreadsheet with initial credit math), postmortem-outline.md, drive link with requested logs.

Next steps:
- Ben: please confirm whether the proposed 15% goodwill credit is acceptable to finance or whether we should propose a different fixed amount ahead of the DocuSign.
- Samira/Gordon: please confirm tenant IDs (or share logs) so we can finalize the pro-rated calculation by EOD tomorrow.
- I'll schedule a 30-min executive sync for tomorrow 10:00 PST to walk through the RCA timeline and the commercial calculation.

We're committed to making Meadow whole and to tightening our operational controls so this does not recur. If you'd prefer a call now rather than tomorrow, I'm available.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
Irene.Choi@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0124
